title: Find the yellow-violet-red resistor
story: A 12 V circuit needs a resistor that lets about 2.5 mA flow. The schematic says 4k7, and the bag of loose resistors on your desk has no labels, only color bands: brown-black-red, red-red-red, yellow-violet-red, yellow-violet-orange, and brown-black-orange. Decode the bands and drop the right one in the slot so the current lands between 2.3 mA and 2.8 mA.
hints: Yellow is 4, violet is 7, and a red third band means 'add two zeros'.
Check with Ohm's law: 12 V / 4700 ohm = ?
